baseline_runs.answer:
- Inflation means that over time, things cost more money. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your grandparents were kids might cost $1.50 today.

- It happens because prices go up little by little each year, so the same dollar can buy a little less than it could before.

- People usually keep an eye on inflation so that wages and savings can keep up, which helps make sure your money still buys what you need.

- Inflation means prices slowly go up over time. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your grandparents were kids might cost a dollar or more today.

- Money loses a little bit of its buying power when this happens. That means your $5 can buy fewer snacks than it could before, even though the bill looks exactly the same.

- A little inflation is normal and healthy for an economy, but if prices rise too fast, it becomes hard for families to afford everyday things, so governments and banks work to keep it slow and steady.

- **Definition:** Inflation is the sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services over time, which means each unit of currency buys fewer goods and services.

- **Causes:** It typically results from demand-pull factors (spending outpacing supply), cost-push factors (rising production costs such as wages or energy), or an expansion of the money supply.

- **Effects:** Moderate inflation can encourage spending and investment, but high or unpredictable inflation erodes savings and fixed incomes, distorts planning, and is often managed by central banks through interest rate adjustments.

- **Definition:** Inflation is the sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services over time, which means each unit of currency buys fewer goods and services.

- **Common causes:** It typically arises from demand-pull factors (spending outpacing supply), cost-push factors (rising production costs such as wages or energy), or an expansion of the money supply.

- **Effects and measurement:** Moderate inflation is often considered normal in growing economies, but high or unpredictable inflation erodes savings and fixed incomes, and it is commonly tracked with indices like the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

ablations.prompt: Explain inflation to a 10 year old.

runs.answer:
Imagine you have $5, and you go to the store to buy a candy bar that costs $5. You can get exactly one.

Now imagine a year later, and that same candy bar costs $6. Your $5 still looks the same, but it can't buy the candy bar anymore. Your money got a little weaker, because things got more expensive.

That's inflation: when prices go up over time, each dollar you have can buy less stuff than it could before.

Why do prices go up? Sometimes lots of people want to buy the same things, but there aren't enough of those things to go around, so stores raise their prices. Sometimes it costs more to make things, like when the ingredients for the candy bar get more expensive, so the store passes that cost on to you.

Grown-ups keep an eye on inflation because if prices go up too fast, it gets hard for families to afford what they need. But a little bit of inflation is normal, kind of like how you grow a little bit every year.

Imagine you have $5, and you want to buy a candy bar that costs $5. You can buy it, no problem.

Now imagine that next year, the same candy bar costs $6. Your $5 is still $5, but it can't buy as much as it could before. You can only get a little less stuff with the same money. That's basically what inflation is: prices going up over time, so each dollar buys a little less than it used to.

Why do prices go up? Sometimes lots of people want to buy the same things, and there aren't quite enough to go around, so stores can charge more. Sometimes it costs more to make things, like when ingredients or gas get more expensive, and companies pass that cost on to you.

Usually inflation goes up slowly, like a little bit each year. That's normal. If prices went up really fast, that would be a big problem, because people's money would lose its value quickly, and it would be hard to save up for things.

So the simple version: inflation is when stuff gets more expensive, and your money doesn't stretch as far as it used to.
